back2basics.concept: Free Trade Agreement and Trade Facilitation
back2basics.text: A Free Trade Agreement (FTA) is a pact between countries to reduce or eliminate tariffs and trade barriers to encourage trade. Trade facilitation involves simplifying and harmonizing international trade procedures, often through digitalisation, to make cross-border trade faster, cheaper, and more predictable. Electronic exchange of origin data helps verify the country of origin of goods, enabling preferential tariff treatment under FTAs.

2026-10-22-pm-266ecfee0d.deck: India and New Zealand signed a Memorandum of Cooperation (MoC) on Electronic Origin Data Exchange to facilitate bilateral trade under their Free Trade Agreement (FTA) effective from October 20, 2026. This MoC aims to deepen customs cooperation and improve trade facilitation by enabling advance electronic exchange of origin data for goods traded between the two countries.

body.label: Duty-Free Access
body.text: India gains duty-free access to 100% of New Zealand’s tariff lines, a unique feature among India’s trade deals.

body.label: Sectoral Benefits
body.text: Tariffs on sectors like textiles, apparel, leather, engineering goods, plastics, rubber, electronics, pharmaceuticals, agriculture, marine products, and chemicals have been reduced or eliminated.

body.label: Investment Promotion
body.text: New Zealand commits to promoting foreign direct investment (FDI) into India with a target of increasing investment by USD 20 billion within 15 years.

body.label: Mobility Provisions
body.text: Includes new Temporary Employment Entry visa categories, expanded post-study work rights for Indian graduates, guaranteed work rights during study, and a working holiday scheme for Indian nationals.

body.label: New Zealand Market Access
body.text: India grants phased market access on 70% of tariff lines to New Zealand, excluding sensitive sectors like dairy and certain agricultural products.

Auctions are the process through which these securities are sold to investors, often involving Primary Dealers who have underwriting commitments to ensure the auction's success. back2basics.concept: Judicial oversight and procedural fairness in investigations
back2basics.text: In India, the judiciary ensures that investigations by police and agencies comply with legal procedures and respect constitutional rights. Courts can stay investigations if due process is not followed, such as when accused persons are not heard or proper approvals are missing. Agencies like the Enforcement Directorate (ED) and state police have distinct roles and powers defined by statutes like the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. Judicial review maintains the balance of power and protects individuals from arbitrary action.

This development highlights issues of judicial oversight, procedural fairness, and the limits of investigative agencies under Indian law, relevant for governance and accountability topics in UPSC.

body.label: Stay on investigation
body.text: The Supreme Court stayed the Kerala Police investigation into the FIR against former CM Pinarayi Vijayan and his family for seven days, while maintaining the FIR itself.

body.label: Case sent back to High Court
body.text: The apex court set aside the Kerala High Court Division Bench order and directed it to hear the appeals filed by Vijayan and others against the FIR registration.

body.label: FIR registration questioned
body.text: The petitioners argued they were not made parties nor heard before the FIR was ordered by the Kerala High Court Single Judge Bench.

body.label: No opinion on ECIR
body.text: The Supreme Court did not comment on the Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) registered against the petitioners but allowed them to challenge it in the appropriate forum.

sections.heading: What is the Supreme Court's order in the CMRL-Exalogic case?

body.label: Procedural fairness emphasized
body.text: The Court emphasized principles of natural justice, noting that even high-profile individuals must be subject to rule of law and proper procedure.

body.label: Limits of ED's power under PMLA
body.text: The Court clarified that Section 66(2) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) is an intimation, not a mandate, and the decision to register an FIR lies with the police.

body.label: No super-administrator role for PMLA
body.text: The Court stated the PMLA cannot assume all investigative powers and should not interfere with statutory domains of other agencies.

body.label: Requirement of prior government approval
body.text: The Court questioned whether the Kerala Police sought prior approval under Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, before investigating a former Chief Minister.

body.label: New criminal procedure provisions
body.text: The Court noted that under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), a Magistrate must hear an accused public servant before investigation, unlike the repealed Code of Criminal Procedure.

sections.heading: Why did the Supreme Court intervene in the investigation?

body.label: Judicial oversight of investigations
body.text: The Supreme Court's intervention shows the judiciary's role in ensuring investigations follow due process and respect legal limits.

body.label: Balance between agencies
body.text: The case highlights the need to balance powers between agencies like the ED and state police to prevent overreach.

body.label: Protection of rights of accused
body.text: The stay protects the rights of accused persons, ensuring they are heard before investigations proceed.

back2basics.text: Cooperative federalism is a concept where the Union and State governments work together to achieve common goals while respecting each other's constitutional powers and autonomy. It involves consultation, coordination, and shared responsibility rather than uniformity in all matters. This approach helps balance national objectives with regional diversity, especially in legislative and administrative functions.

2026-10-22-pm-e905937155.deck: The 23rd Law Commission of India organised a National Conference on 22 October 2026 to discuss cooperative federalism and law reforms involving State Law Commissions and national legal experts. This event highlights the constitutional balance of legislative powers and the need for coordinated legal reforms between the Centre and States, a key topic for UPSC exams.

body.label: Conference objective

body.label: Participants involved

body.label: Key themes

sections.heading: What was the purpose of the National Conference on Cooperative Federalism and Law Reforms?

body.label: Vice-President's emphasis

body.label: Cooperative federalism clarified

body.label: Union Minister's priorities

body.label: Law Commission Chairperson's proposal

back2basics.text: Monsoon rainfall in India is influenced by low-pressure systems that form over the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea, bringing moisture and storms. The India Meteorological Department issues weather alerts such as orange and yellow to warn about heavy rainfall and potential hazards like landslips. Orange alerts indicate very heavy rainfall and higher risk, while yellow alerts indicate isolated heavy rain with moderate risk.

2026-10-22-pm-f04422f7a3.deck: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued orange and yellow alerts for several districts in Kerala amid heavy rain and landslip warnings triggered by low-pressure systems over the Bay of Bengal. body: These systems cause moisture influx leading to heavy rainfall and thunderstorms, especially in southern states like Kerala.
The India Meteorological Department issues alerts such as orange and yellow to warn about expected heavy rain and associated risks.
Such alerts enable timely government and public response to reduce damage from floods and landslips.
Understanding these weather patterns is essential for disaster preparedness and climate-related studies.
structure.conclusion: Thus, Bay of Bengal low-pressure systems and weather alerts play a critical role in monsoon dynamics and disaster management.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the recent weather alerts in Kerala:
1. Orange alerts were issued for Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, and Pathanamthitta districts due to very heavy rainfall.
2. The low-pressure area responsible formed over the Arabian Sea near the Somalia coast.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 2 is incorrect because the low-pressure area causing heavy rain formed over the southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining Tamil Nadu coast, not the Arabian Sea near Somalia.

body.label: Low-pressure systems
body.text: A low-pressure area formed over the southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining Tamil Nadu coast, causing moisture influx and heavy thunderstorms in Kerala.

body.label: Cyclonic circulation effect
body.text: The cyclonic circulation associated with the low-pressure area supports isolated to very heavy thunderstorms along Kerala's ghat regions and southern and central parts.

body.label: Upcoming intensification
body.text: Another low-pressure area expected around October 23 is likely to intensify and increase rainfall activity across Kerala from October 23 to 25.

body.text: On October 21, orange alerts were issued for Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, and Kottayam due to very heavy rainfall.

body.label: Yellow alert districts
body.text: Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Palakkad, and Malappuram were placed under yellow alert for isolated heavy rainfall.

body.label: Next day alerts
body.text: On October 22, orange alerts were issued for Ernakulam, Thrissur, Malappuram, and Kozhikode, with the rest of Kerala under yellow alert.

back2basics.concept: Data breach and cybersecurity in banking
back2basics.text: A data breach occurs when sensitive, protected or confidential data is accessed or disclosed without authorization. In banking, this can expose customer personal information, increasing risks of fraud and identity theft. Cybersecurity involves protecting systems and data from such unauthorized access. Banks follow protocols to detect, respond to, and notify stakeholders about breaches to safeguard customer interests and maintain trust.

2026-10-22-pm-f92931e2b1.deck: In October 2026, State Bank of India (SBI) disclosed that about 3,897 customer records with personally identifiable information were found on the dark web. This incident highlights cybersecurity challenges in banking and the need for stronger data protection and customer notification mechanisms.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the SBI data breach reported in October 2026:
1. SBI itself detected the data breach and immediately informed all affected customers.
2. The data breach involved exposure of personally identifiable information of nearly 3,900 customers on the dark web.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 1 is incorrect because SBI learned of the breach from external agencies and did not immediately inform affected customers; statement 2 is correct as per the reported data.

body.label: Data exposure details
body.text: SBI found 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information such as mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, email addresses, residential addresses, and loan-related metadata exposed on the dark web.

body.label: Source of alert
body.text: The bank received alerts from its Threat Intelligence Service Provider, Defence Cyber Agency, and CERT-In about the suspected data exposure five days before disclosure.

body.label: Investigation and response
body.text: SBI activated cyber incident response protocols and engaged an independent CERT-In-empanelled cybersecurity agency to assess the breach's nature and extent.

body.label: Impact on operations
body.text: SBI stated the breach did not materially impact its core business operations, financial performance, or business continuity.

sections.heading: What happened in the SBI data breach?

body.label: Customer risk
body.text: Exposed customers are vulnerable to fraud as attackers can impersonate SBI officials using leaked personal details.

body.label: Notification gap
body.text: SBI did not inform affected customers directly, as current laws require notification only to regulators, not customers, until May 2027 when new data protection provisions come into effect.

body.label: Calls for stronger rules
body.text: The Internet Freedom Foundation urged SBI to notify affected customers immediately and demanded regulatory changes to mandate customer notification of data breaches.

sections.heading: Why does this data breach matter for cybersecurity and governance?

body.label: Customer precautions
body.text: Customers should be alert to phishing calls or messages from fraudsters posing as bank officials using their leaked data.

body.label: Regulatory action
body.text: The Internet Freedom Foundation requested the Reserve Bank of India to require all regulated entities to notify customers of data breaches promptly.

body.label: Legal enforcement
body.text: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology should bring into force the data breach notification provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act and Rules without delay.
